wins.text: Full year net income of $57.5B, EPS of $20.18, revenue of $185B, and ROTCE of 20% (excluding significant items)
Equities Markets revenue up 40% YoY with robust performance across the franchise, particularly in Prime; Fixed Income up 7% YoY
AWM revenue of $6.5B up 13% YoY; record client asset net inflows of $553B for the year; long-term net inflows of $209B for the full year
CCB added 1.7M net new checking accounts, 10.4M new card accounts, and record households in wealth management for the full year
CET1 ratio of 14.5% with Jamie Dimon noting $30-40B+ of excess capital, supporting continued capital distributions

risks.text: Apple Card portfolio reserve build of $2.2B in CCB impacted Q4 net income; advanced RWA contribution of ~$110B at closing (expected to reduce to ~$30B near term), adding integration complexity over a 2-year timeline

Potential credit card APR caps floated via social media post by the President; management acknowledged this would be 'very dramatic' for the industry, reduce credit access broadly, and present 'significant challenge' to JPM's card business
IB fees down 5% YoY in Q4 reflecting strong prior-year compare and deal timing pushouts; management cautious on fee outlook given exceptionally strong 2025 base
Consumer deposit growth expected to be lower than the 6% Investor Day scenario; balance-per-account inflection pushed out to H2 2026 due to persistent yield-seeking flows
Stablecoin/GENIUS Act legislation poses potential systemic risk to bank deposits; ABA estimates up to $6.6T of deposits at risk if interest-bearing stablecoin loophole is not closed

guidance_items.detail: NII ex Markets expected to be ~$95B for 2026; total NII expected to be ~$103B, with Markets NII increasing to ~$8B
No explicit EPS guide provided; ROTCE framed as an output of business strategy rather than a hard target
2026 adjusted expense expected to be ~$105B, up ~$9B YoY, driven by volume/revenue-related costs, compensation, tech, and Apple Card integration
2026 card net charge-off rate expected to be ~3.4%, reflecting favorable delinquency trends and continued consumer resilience
Card loan growth expected at ~6-7% for 2026, lower than recent years as revolve normalization tailwind fades; modest firm-wide deposit growth anticipated

analyst_concerns_not_in_prepared: Stablecoin/GENIUS Act deposit risk and JPM's strategic positioning — management did not proactively address this in prepared remarks
Potential executive-imposed credit card APR caps — not mentioned in prepared remarks despite being a major investor concern over the weekend prior to the call
Specifics of tech and AI spending levels for 2026 — management discussed expense growth thematically but declined to break out AI/tech spend in prepared remarks
